Purdue Boilermakers.previous_hc_experience: Yes, though the guide addresses it indirectly — it records offensive line coach Vance Vice having come with Barry Odom from UNLV, which is where Odom coached before Purdue.
Purdue Boilermakers.dc: Kevin Kane, previously Purdue's coordinator under Ryan Walters in 2023 and 2024, returning after a season coaching Minnesota's linebackers.
Purdue Boilermakers.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Purdue Boilermakers.dc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator, and the guide records Kane taking over.
Purdue Boilermakers.play_caller: Kevin Kane on defense, and the guide treats the arrangement as changed: he now has more autonomy calling the defense than he had under Ryan Walters.
Purdue Boilermakers.offensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
Purdue Boilermakers.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme, but a stated preference is recorded: Kane prefers to attack more than Walters did.
Purdue Boilermakers.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated philosophy. The guide records Purdue struggling particularly in short yardage, 85th on third downs, and in the red zone, 119th.
Purdue Boilermakers.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide notes no portal quarterback was added, so the job is Ryan Browne's again, and holds him to improvement while noting fairly that he had little help and played through an ankle injury.
Purdue Boilermakers.continuity: Head coach, offensive coordinator and quarterback return; the defensive coordinator changes. The Stability Score table (p. 44) prints 4, 3, 0 and 4, plus 2 for 11 returning starters, totalling 13.
Purdue Boilermakers.staff_turnover: Two specific changes the guide records. Odom fired offensive line coach Vance Vice, who had come with him from UNLV, and hired Zach Crabtree, previously with coordinator Josh Henson at USC — a change the guide rates an upgrade. Kevin Kane takes over the defense.
Purdue Boilermakers.prior_school: UNLV for Vice, USC for Crabtree and Henson, and Minnesota for Kane's most recent job. On the roster the guide records Fame Ijeboi from Minnesota, Jerrick Gibson from Texas, Travis Terrell from Jackson State, Bisi Owens from Penn, Assad Wassem from Florida Atlantic, Xavier Townsend from Iowa State, Boaz Stanley from South Carolina, Micah Banuelos from USC and Nuki Mafi from Oklahoma State.
Purdue Boilermakers.portal_recruiting: The main mechanism for improvement. The guide expects most offensive production to come from portal additions, names three portal receivers all expected to start, and records as many as four new portal starters possible on the offensive line.
Purdue Boilermakers.vsin_assessment: Process credited, results not. The guide separates the two explicitly: Purdue is in better shape with more continuity than before Odom arrived and the staff is better, but the talent still cannot compete weekly in the Big Ten. It records an 18-game Big Ten losing streak and no Power Four wins across two years, and rates Odom and staff an upgrade on Ryan Walters' tenure while being candid that Purdue is far from the competitiveness of the Jeff Brohm years.
Purdue Boilermakers.strengths: A staff the guide rates better than its predecessor with more continuity, an offensive line coaching change it calls an upgrade, a rebuilt and larger offensive line, and a defensive coordinator with more autonomy and a more aggressive stated preference.
Purdue Boilermakers.concerns: Improvement of only one win, an 18-game conference losing streak, a coordinator whose previous Purdue units finished last in the league in most defensive categories, and a roster the guide says cannot compete weekly at this level.
Purdue Boilermakers.betting: Recommendation is Over 3.5 wins, and the coaching link is the stated basis: the guide rates Odom and staff an upgrade on Ryan Walters' tenure while conceding Purdue is far from the Jeff Brohm years.

Rutgers Scarlet Knights.previous_hc_experience: Yes, at the same programme. The guide records Greg Schiano taking Rutgers near the top of the Big East in the late 2000s in his first spell, and being 31-41 across six Big Ten seasons in this one.
Rutgers Scarlet Knights.dc: Travis Johansen, hired after taking South Dakota to the FCS playoffs.
Rutgers Scarlet Knights.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Rutgers Scarlet Knights.dc_status: New — the guide records Johansen's hire, and the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Rutgers Scarlet Knights.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name. The guide records that Schiano will stay involved on defense as always, but that Johansen gets more autonomy than his predecessors.
Rutgers Scarlet Knights.offensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide's stated tactical requirement is that Schiano and Ciarrocca must play more ball control given the defensive problems.
Rutgers Scarlet Knights.defensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
Rutgers Scarlet Knights.tempo: Addressed indirectly through the ball-control requirement.
Rutgers Scarlet Knights.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split beyond the call for more ball control.
Rutgers Scarlet Knights.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide expects Boston College transfer Dylan Lonergan — 66.9% for 2,025 yards with 12 touchdowns to five interceptions across nine starts, and once a four-star taken to Alabama by Nick Saban — to win the job over sophomore AJ Surace.
Rutgers Scarlet Knights.continuity: Head coach and offensive coordinator return; the defensive coordinator and quarterback both change. The Stability Score table (p. 44) prints 4, 3, 0 and 0, plus 2 for 12 returning starters, totalling 9.
Rutgers Scarlet Knights.staff_turnover: Concentrated on defense and the offensive line. Travis Johansen arrives as coordinator and recruits from his own FCS network, bringing Drake head coach Joe Woodley to coach rush ends and Drake coordinator Adam Cox for the safeties. Jim Turner replaces Pat Flaherty on the offensive line; the guide records that Turner was most recently interim head coach of the UFL's Memphis Showboats before the franchise folded, and that he has a checkered past, having been fired as Miami Dolphins offensive line coach over a pattern of harassment and bullying.
Rutgers Scarlet Knights.prior_school: South Dakota and Drake for the new defensive staff. On the roster the guide records Dylan Lonergan from Boston College, Hank Zilinskas from Colorado, Everett Small from Eastern Michigan and Isaiah Cook from Delaware State.
Rutgers Scarlet Knights.portal_recruiting: Framed as both a weakness and the method. The guide says Rutgers consistently has player retention problems because of NIL, while noting it kept Antwan Raymond and K.J. Duff, and records that Rutgers is rebuilding the defense through the portal for a second straight season, leaving open whether this attempt goes better.
Rutgers Scarlet Knights.vsin_assessment: Sympathetic to the constraint, firm about the deadline. The guide gives credence to the view that Schiano coaches with an arm tied behind his back, because Rutgers has not made the financial investment needed to compete in the Big Ten — while stating that results must eventually come.
Rutgers Scarlet Knights.strengths: A long-tenured head coach the guide says operates under structural disadvantage, offensive-coordinator continuity, retained skill talent in a 1,275-yard rusher and a 1,084-yard receiver, and a defensive coordinator given more autonomy than his predecessors.
Rutgers Scarlet Knights.concerns: A defense that allowed 432.9 yards per game, 125th in FBS and the worst of any Power Four team, with only three starters back; a second consecutive portal defensive rebuild; three open offensive line spots; and an offensive line coach the guide records as having a checkered past.
Rutgers Scarlet Knights.betting: Recommendation is Over 4.5 wins. The coaching link is the offensive side: even with the defensive problems the guide expects points, with Lonergan likely to win the job alongside Raymond and Duff.

UCLA Bruins.previous_hc_experience: Extensive at lower levels, and central to the case for him. The Coaching Carousel records a career 132-52 record, Holy Cross before James Madison, and taking JMU to the College Football Playoff as the Group of Five representative last season. The team pages add five FCS playoff appearances in seven years at Holy Cross.
UCLA Bruins.oc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
UCLA Bruins.dc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
UCLA Bruins.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
UCLA Bruins.offensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide characterises the staff by its output — the nation's 16th-ranked offense at James Madison at 452.6 yards per game — and records a stylistic point about the quarterback: Nico Iamaleava is most effective throwing on the run rather than from the pocket, so receivers must create separation.
UCLA Bruins.defensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
UCLA Bruins.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split.
UCLA Bruins.qb_development: Addressed as an expectation rather than a record. The guide's starting point is that Iamaleava stayed and now works with a staff that produced the nation's 16th-ranked offense at James Madison, and it balances his disappointing 1,929 passing yards in 11 starts against 64.4% completions, seven interceptions and 505 rushing yards.
UCLA Bruins.continuity: Broken on the staff, intact at quarterback. The Stability Score table (p. 44) prints 0 for the head coach, 0 for the offensive coordinator, 0 for the defensive coordinator and 4 for the quarterback, plus 4 for 18 returning starters, totalling 8.
UCLA Bruins.staff_turnover: Complete at the top and replaced en bloc. Chesney brought eight assistants from James Madison including coordinators Dean Kennedy and Colin Hitschler.
UCLA Bruins.prior_school: James Madison, extensively — eight assistants, both coordinators, and 10 of his 42 transfers including all-purpose back Wayne Knight, receiver Landon Ellis and edge Aiden Gobaira. Other additions recorded are Brian Rowe from South Carolina, Leland Smith from San Jose State, Sahir West and Samuel Omosigho from Oklahoma.
UCLA Bruins.portal_recruiting: Explicitly modelled on a precedent. The Coaching Carousel notes the hire of former James Madison head coach Curt Cignetti seemed to work out at Indiana and that the Bruins' athletic department is hoping for the same. The team pages record 42 transfers, 10 of them from JMU, and the guide names the hope directly — that Westwood repeats what Cignetti did in Bloomington.
UCLA Bruins.vsin_assessment: Strongly positive on the hire, cautious on the price. The Coaching Carousel calls Chesney a winner and a strong hire by all accounts, notes that for a Bruins side that has finished a season ranked only once since 2014 the bar is not terribly high, and says he has the chance to rapidly improve the programme even with a tough Big Ten schedule. The team pages rate Chesney and his staff a massive upgrade on Deshaun Foster's group.
UCLA Bruins.strengths: A 132-52 career record and a College Football Playoff appearance at the Group of Five level, a coordinator pair transplanted from a top-20 offense, a returning quarterback, 18 returning starters, three returning offensive line starters, and a secondary the guide says will be good again.
UCLA Bruins.concerns: A pass rush that produced 10 sacks, the worst in FBS, masked by that secondary; 33.4 points allowed per game, 125th nationally; an essentially new receiving corps with no established No. 1; and the step up from the Sun Belt to the Big Ten.
UCLA Bruins.betting: Recommendation is Under 6.5 wins, and the guide is explicit that this is not a verdict on the coach: it rates Chesney and his staff a massive upgrade and still calls the team a bit overpriced.
UCLA Bruins.carousel_summary: Adam Burke opens on the precedent: the hire of former James Madison head coach Curt Cignetti seemed to work out at Indiana, and now the Bruins' athletic department is hoping for the same with Chesney, who was at Holy Cross prior to his two seasons with the Dukes. He states the record plainly — Chesney is a winner with a career 132-52 record and took JMU to the College Football Playoff as the G5 representative last season. He then sets the bar: for a Bruins bunch that has only finished the season ranked one time since 2014, the bar isn't terribly high, so Chesney, a strong hire by all accounts, has the chance to rapidly improve the programme, even with a tough Big Ten schedule.

USC Trojans.previous_hc_experience: Yes for both the head coach and the incoming coordinator. The guide records Lincoln Riley reaching the playoff three times at Oklahoma, and identifies Gary Patterson as the former TCU head coach.
USC Trojans.dc: Gary Patterson, the former TCU head coach, lured from semi-retirement after D'Anton Lynn returned to his alma mater Penn State.
USC Trojans.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
USC Trojans.dc_status: New — the guide records Patterson becoming the third coordinator in four seasons, and the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
USC Trojans.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
USC Trojans.offensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide expects plenty of points as always under Riley, and draws a tactical consequence from the receiving losses — the Trojans may run more with King Miller and Waymond Jordan behind a line returning all five starters.
USC Trojans.defensive_scheme: Named, and changing. The guide records Patterson switching to a 4-2-5 with depth up front.
USC Trojans.run_pass: Addressed as an expected shift toward the run, driven by the loss of Makai Lemon and Ja'Kobi Lane and a receiving group the guide judges slightly below USC's usual level.
USC Trojans.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide records Jayden Maiava returning within what may be Riley's most talented group in five seasons.
USC Trojans.continuity: Head coach, offensive coordinator and quarterback return; the defensive coordinator changes for the third time in four seasons. The Stability Score table (p. 44) prints 4, 3, 0 and 4, plus 4 for 17 returning starters, totalling 15.
USC Trojans.staff_turnover: Confined to the defensive coordinator, but the guide treats it as consequential: D'Anton Lynn left for Penn State after genuine improvement, and Patterson has not coached full-time in nearly four years.
USC Trojans.prior_school: TCU for Patterson. On the roster the guide records Alex VanSumeren from Michigan State and Terrell Anderson from NC State.
USC Trojans.portal_recruiting: Tied to the head coach's record. The guide records the nation's No. 1 recruiting class alongside 14 returning starters.
USC Trojans.vsin_assessment: Expectation corrected, and one hire singled out as a gamble. The guide notes that when Riley was hired the media question was how many national titles he would win, not whether, and corrects it — he must first reach the playoff, which he did three times at Oklahoma. It records him halfway through a ten-year, $110 million contract and frames the Patterson hire as a gamble he needs to pay off, while flagging concern about a new coordinator installing a new system.
USC Trojans.strengths: Possibly Riley's most talented group in five seasons, 14 returning starters and the nation's No. 1 recruiting class, an offensive line returning all five starters, a returning quarterback and offensive coordinator, and documented defensive improvement to build on — 51st in scoring defense, 47th against the pass, 58th against the run.
USC Trojans.concerns: A third defensive coordinator in four seasons installing a new 4-2-5, a coordinator who has not coached full-time in nearly four years, a run defense that ranked 12th in the conference, replacing 1,900 receiving yards and All-American Bishop Fitzgerald, and a 5-11 record against ranked opposition with a 10-10 mark in true Big Ten road games under Riley.
USC Trojans.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit coaching-driven market argument. Its coaching-linked expectation is directional: plenty of points as always under Riley, with concern about a new coordinator installing a new system.

Washington Huskies.oc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Washington Huskies.dc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Washington Huskies.offensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme. The guide records Washington finishing fourth nationally in scoring at 34.1 points and fifth in total offense at 409.9 yards.
Washington Huskies.defensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
Washington Huskies.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated philosophy.
Washington Huskies.qb_development: Not addressed as a coaching record. The guide's quarterback material is about commitment and performance level: Demond Williams Jr is among the conference's more dynamic quarterbacks, and must be better against better teams, having managed 645 yards with three touchdowns and six interceptions across Washington's four defeats.
Washington Huskies.continuity: Head coach, defensive coordinator and quarterback return; the offensive coordinator changes. The Stability Score table (p. 44) prints 4, 0, 3 and 4, plus 3 for 14 returning starters, totalling 14.
Washington Huskies.staff_turnover: Not addressed in guide beyond the offensive coordinator point printed in the Stability Score table.
Washington Huskies.prior_school: Not addressed in guide for the staff. On the roster the guide records Jayden Limar from Oregon and Trey Cooley from Troy.
Washington Huskies.portal_recruiting: Dominated in the guide by a retention episode. It records that days after signing a $4 million NIL deal to return, Williams entered the transfer portal and was reportedly close to signing for more money with LSU; it did not reach court, and he returned to Seattle. The guide treats NIL and the portal as simply how the sport now works while noting this came perilously close to his leaving with lawyers about to be involved, and suggests he received bad advice from his representatives. It separately records Washington's highest-rated recruiting class in school history, including four-star receivers Jordan Clay, Mason James and Trez Davis, and five-star freshman Kodi Greene expected at left tackle.
Washington Huskies.vsin_assessment: Progress acknowledged, the last step identified. The guide credits Jedd Fisch with improving Washington from 6-7 to 9-4 in his second season and says the team has reached the upper level of the Big Ten in his third year, with the requirement now being to beat the league's elite. Its counterweight is specific: against the four best defenses Washington faced — Ohio State, Michigan, Wisconsin and Oregon — the Huskies averaged 9.3 points and 4.3 yards per play. It records that Washington is still looking for a signature win to convince its support of Fisch, at 2-7 in Big Ten road games under him.
Washington Huskies.strengths: Year-on-year improvement under the head coach, 65% of production returning, a retained quarterback the guide calls among the conference's more dynamic, defensive-coordinator continuity, four returning offensive line starters, and the highest-rated recruiting class in school history.
Washington Huskies.concerns: A new offensive coordinator, an offense that averaged 9.3 points against the four best defenses it faced, a 2-7 record in Big Ten road games under Fisch with trips to USC, Oregon and Nebraska to come, and a running back room where the three experienced additions and returnees all missed spring with injuries.
Washington Huskies.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit coaching-driven market argument.

Wisconsin Badgers.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Wisconsin Badgers.dc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Wisconsin Badgers.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Wisconsin Badgers.offensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme, but a stated direction is recorded: coordinator Jeff Grimes is expected to go run-heavy, especially with a mobile quarterback, though the guide insists some receiver production is still required.
Wisconsin Badgers.defensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme. The guide records Wisconsin ranking 24th nationally in total defense despite being on the field constantly because of the offense.
Wisconsin Badgers.run_pass: Stated as run-heavy in intent, against a programme identity the results contradict: the guide notes Wisconsin's identity has always been power running, yet it ranked 115th nationally at 116.7 yards per game.
Wisconsin Badgers.qb_development: Not addressed as a record, and the guide records the opposite pattern: for the fourth straight year the starting quarterback comes from the portal, this time Sun Belt Player of the Year Colton Joseph from Old Dominion.
Wisconsin Badgers.continuity: Head coach and both coordinators return; the quarterback changes. The Stability Score table (p. 44) prints 4, 3, 3 and 0, plus 2 for 10 returning starters, totalling 12.
Wisconsin Badgers.staff_turnover: Not addressed in guide. The Stability Score table records both coordinators returning.
Wisconsin Badgers.prior_school: Not addressed in guide for the staff. On the roster the guide records Colton Joseph from Old Dominion, Shamar Rigby from Oklahoma State, Malachi Coleman from Minnesota, Abu Sama III from Iowa State, Bryan Jackson II from USC, Marvin Burks Jr from Missouri, Javan Robinson from Arizona State, Cai Bates from Florida State and Eric Fletcher from East Carolina.
Wisconsin Badgers.portal_recruiting: Heavy, and the guide reads it as a symptom. It records a complete roster makeover with 33 transfers, a fourth straight portal starting quarterback, and a secondary that is entirely portal additions apart from Matthew Jung — then judges that the heavy portal reliance looks like a search for a quick fix.
Wisconsin Badgers.vsin_assessment: The hottest seat in the conference, stated as such. The guide records that Luke Fickell was expected to restore the Barry Alvarez era and has instead gone 7-6, 5-7 and 4-8, and says no Big Ten seat is hotter. It supplies the starkest single number as its evidence: Wisconsin scored 81 points across nine Big Ten games in 2025, the worst scoring offense in the Power Four at 12.8 points per game, 133rd nationally.
Wisconsin Badgers.strengths: Full coordinator continuity, a defense that ranked 24th nationally in total defense while being on the field constantly, two productive returning linebackers who contributed heavily as freshmen, three returning offensive line starters, and a Sun Belt Player of the Year at quarterback the guide sees as a potential jolt.
Wisconsin Badgers.concerns: Three consecutive declining seasons, the worst scoring offense in the Power Four, a run game ranked 115th nationally against a programme identity built on power running, almost no returning receiver production, and a roster the guide says lacks talent at many positions.
Wisconsin Badgers.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit market recommendation tied to coaching. Its coaching-linked judgement is that Joseph certainly makes the offense better but the ceiling stays low, and that seven wins is a big ask despite the easier schedule.
